title: Persistence Properties of a Phase-ordering System with Competing Dynamics
abstract: We investigate the persistence properties during phase ordering in the two-dimensional ($d=2$) Ising model evolving under competing nonconserved spin-flip and conserved spin-exchange dynamics by means of Monte Carlo simulations at zero temperature. We examine three distinct persistence probabilities: (i) the total persistence probability, defined as the probability that a lattice site has never experienced a change in the sign of the spin residing there; (ii) the spin-flip persistence probability, which exclusively measures the fraction of sites that have never undergone a spin-flip event; and (iii) the composite persistence probability, defined as the fraction of sites that have experienced neither a spin-flip nor a spin-exchange event. In the asymptotic regime, both the total and spin-flip persistence probabilities exhibit identical power-law decay, irrespective of the relative occurrence probability of the spin-flip move $p_r$. The corresponding persistence exponent $θ_i \approx 0.225$, is found to be consistent with the value reported for systems evolving purely under nonconserved dynamics. We further demonstrate that both persistence measures satisfy the scaling relation $d-d_f^i=θ_i/α_i$, where $d_f^i$ is the fractal dimension of the corresponding persistence lattice and $α_i\approx 1/2$ characterizes the asymptotic power-law growth of spatially correlated regions of non-persistent spins. In contrast, although the composite persistence probability also exhibits asymptotic power-law decay, both the corresponding persistence exponent $θ_{\rm c}$ and the fractal dimension $d_f^{\rm c}$ of the persistence lattice show strong dependence on $p_r$. Combined with the presence of a universal growth exponent $α_{\rm c}\approx 1/2$, this leads to the breakdown of the scaling relation among the characteristic exponents for the composite persistence.
summary: This work analyzes the persistence properties during phase ordering in an Ising model subjected to competing spin-flip and spin-exchange dynamics at zero temperature. While standard measures of persistence retain universal scaling behavior consistent with nonconserved dynamics, the composite measure reveals a strong, non-universal dependence on the competition parameter $p_r$, highlighting distinct physical consequences for different types of memory.
main_problem: The study investigates how persistence properties change during phase ordering when a system evolves under competing dynamics involving both nonconserved (spin-flip) and conserved (spin-exchange) interactions.
main_result: For total and spin-flip persistence, the exponents remain universal and consistent with purely nonconserved dynamics; however, the composite persistence measure shows strong dependence on the relative probability of the competing moves, breaking expected scaling relations.
method: The analysis relies heavily on Monte Carlo simulations at zero temperature to track time evolution and calculate various persistence probabilities and their associated spatial correlation functions.
model_or_system: The system is a two-dimensional Ising model undergoing phase ordering. The dynamics are mixed, controlled by the probability $p_r$ of executing a nonconserved spin-flip move versus a conserved spin-exchange move.
key_observables: Total persistence probability ($P_t(t)$), spin-flip persistence probability ($P_f(t)$), and composite persistence probability ($P_c(t)$); decay exponents ($	heta_i$); fractal dimensions ($d_i^f$).
important_parameters: The relative probability $p_r$ controlling the competition between dynamics; zero temperature ($T=0$); spatial dimension $d=2$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that asymptotic power-law decay and dynamic scaling forms can be successfully applied to characterize long-time behavior.
figures_summary: Figures show snapshots of domain growth, confirmation of scaling behavior using correlation functions, and double-logarithmic plots demonstrating the collapse of scaled persistence probabilities for different dynamics.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the model and defines three distinct persistence measures. It then analyzes the asymptotic decay and scaling relations for the total and spin-flip measures, finding consistency with known results. Finally, it contrasts this by analyzing the composite measure, demonstrating its unique dependence on $p_r$ and failure to satisfy the established scaling laws.
why_interesting: The study provides a detailed quantitative comparison of how different microscopic dynamics (conserved vs. nonconserved) affect macroscopic memory effects (persistence), which is crucial for understanding relaxation in complex many-body systems relevant to AMO physics or condensed matter modeling.
